title: Token Trace Interaction Matrix — UX notes & sketch backlog (WIP)
content:
Purpose
This doc captures exploratory UX notes, wireframe variants, and a prioritized backlog for a token-level trace + interaction matrix view in the Console. The goal is a compact, queryable surface that lets engineers and product teams: (a) attribute cost to logical operations (prompt, system message, tool call), (b) visualize per-request latency breakdowns across pipeline stages, and (c) quickly find hot tokens or mid-request regressions.

Scope and audience
- Primary: SREs, ML engineers, platform owners who need to debug cost/latency regressions across workloads.
- Secondary: product managers and CS who want per-customer unit economics.
- Out of scope for this phase: deep ML token semantics (no attempt to derive token importance), multi-request aggregated billing export (CSV/GL export is later).

Design goals (ranked)
1) Speed to insight: show attribution within 3 clicks (or two keyboard shortcuts).
2) Density with clarity: pack timeline + cost waterfall + metadata without overwhelming.
3) Low cognitive switching: keep a single canonical drilldown modal so people don't hop between panels.
4) Instrumentation-first: UI must map cleanly to telemetry fields so queries are reproducible.

Primary metrics to measure success
- Time to identify root cause (survey / observation in user testing).
- % of sessions where users open the token drilldown modal (engagement).
- Reduction in number of SRE escalation tickets for opaque per-request cost spikes.

Data assumptions / API contract notes (engineering)
- We'll rely on a per-request trace payload containing: request_id, model_variant, tokens[ {index, text, role, raw_length, cost_usd, token_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit boolean}], stage_timings[ {stage_name, start_ms, end_ms}], and route_tags.
- For large responses (>2048 tokens) server-side sampling will be applied; UI must present sampling indicator and link to full object in raw logs.
- Cost estimates should use the same per-token pricing rules as Billing; UI reads from pricing API rather than local calc to avoid drift.
- Telemetry tags: include stack frame id and batch-id when available to aid correlating with infra metrics.

Sketch / wireframe variants (high level)
Variant A — Compact trace matrix (default)
- Left column: request metadata (request_id, timestamp, model, route, customer tag) with quick actions (open in logs, copy id, pin).
- Center grid: token rows (collapsed by segment: system/prompt/user/assistant/tool) and columns: token index, token text (truncate), token-level cost (USD), token latency (ms), kv cache flag icon. Rows are virtualized for performance.
- Right rail: cost waterfall (stacked bars) showing prompting, generation, tool I/O, and overhead. Hover a token to highlight its contribution in waterfall (animated fade).
- Inline filter bar: role filter (system/user/assistant/tool), latency threshold, cost threshold, and a search by token text or regex.
Strengths: very dense, good for single-request debugging. Weaknesses: can feel cramped for long outputs, token text truncation reduces readability.

Variant B — Timeline + swimlane (expanded)
- Top: condensed timeline showing stage blocks (parse, prompt-compile, batch-queue, generation bursts, tool-call). Each block shows aggregated token latency distribution (mini sparkline).
- Middle: swimlane per-subcomponent (model inference host, cache, network) with colored spans corresponding to where tokens incurred latency. Tokens are rendered horizontally with hover overlays.
- Bottom: cost ledger with line items and attribution to token ranges.
Strengths: better for correlating infra stages to token-level latency. Weaknesses: requires richer telemetry; larger vertical footprint.

Variant C — Comparative matrix (multi-request)
- Two-pane comparison: left is baseline request, right is subject request. Synchronized token alignment (attempt to align by token text or embedding similarity). Diff highlights tokens with >x% cost or latency delta.
- Useful for rollout regressions and A/B variant analysis.
Weaknesses: alignment heuristics may be brittle; higher implementation complexity.

Interaction details (mostly for Variant A)
- Keyboard: J/K to move row focus, Enter to open token drilldown, "f" to open filter palette, "p" to pin a request.
- Hover states: token hover shows small tooltip with full token text, cost breakdown (model, quantization overhead), and links to relevant traces in infra dashboards.
- Click token: opens modal with token history (previous requests where token was expensive), embedding preview, and a button "search for token across customer logs".
- Batch highlights: when a request was batched, show batch-id and offer "jump to batch timeline" that overlays timing across sibling requests.

Token drilldown modal (shared canonical component)
Sections:
  - Header: token text full + copy + occurrences count (how many times in request).
  - Top row: small sparkline of token-latency over token position.
  - Middle: per-host breakdown (rows by GPU host) showing ms and token count.
  - Bottom: quick actions: annotate (internal note), flag for audit, create Jira (pre-filled).
Acceptance criteria for modal:
  - Loads under 300ms for <=512 tokens.
  - Contains linkable permalink for sharing.
  - All numeric fields match telemetry within 1%.

Visual language and affordances
- Color palette: use neutral blues for baseline, amber for high-cost tokens (>2x average), red for extreme latency (>99th).
- Use micro-animations to show token -> waterfall mapping on hover (fade and slight translate) to help visual connection.
- Show small legends inline; avoid separate legend panels.

Backlog grooming (prioritized items)
1) INF-8421 (P0) — Basic Trace Matrix UI (Variant A core) — 5 sp.
   - Virtualized token grid, metadata column, right-side waterfall stub, filters (role, cost, latency), token hover tooltip.
   - Dev notes: endpoint returns first 1024 tokens.
2) INF-8467 (P1) — Token drilldown modal + permalinks — 3 sp.
3) INF-8492 (P1) — Sampling indicator + link to raw trace logs — 2 sp.
4) INF-8540 (P2) — Timeline swimlane prototype (Variant B) — 8 sp.
5) INF-8601 (P2) — Comparative matrix MVP (Variant C) — 8 sp.
6) INF-8675 (P3) — Batch overlay + sibling timelines — 5 sp.
7) INF-8722 (P3) — Billing-pricing API integration (use canonical pricing) — 3 sp.
Estimates are rough; tech leads to review.

Open questions and decisions needed
- Sampling strategy: server should annotate sampled tokens vs full trace. Do we show sampling by default or hide for cleanliness? (ops preference: show).
- Privacy: exposing full token text for customer-owned content — need legal signoff to show plaintext in Console for enterprise plans. Should we mask tokens by default for non-admins?
- Alignment algorithm for comparative view: string match vs embedding-based alignment. Engineering prefers deterministic string-match first.
- Cost rounding: show micro-cost per token (0.00000X) vs aggregated to 4 decimal places. Billing team recommends aggregated to 4 decimals to avoid noise.

Edge cases and performance notes
- Extremely long requests: offer a "condensed mode" that groups contiguous identical-role tokens into a summary row with aggregated cost/latency.
- Low telemetry coverage: if stage timings are missing, UI shows "partial trace" and disables waterfall.
- Mobile: Console will not show token rows on small screens; provide a summarized card view only.

Prototype links and next steps
- Figma: figma:token-trace-matrix-v1 (iterating on hover -> waterfall mapping).
- Next week: design critique with eng (Priya + Owen), bring a small dataset to validate virtualization performance.
- Action items:
  - Marina: consolidate acceptance criteria and hand off to SRE (by 2025-10-09).
  - Diego: spike on sampling UI and API contract (by 2025-10-03).
  - Owen: estimate Variant B implementation effort (by 2025-10-07).

Notes to reviewers
- Testers: when validating, use synthetic traces with clear cost deltas (e.g., insert high-cost special tokens) so hover mapping and waterfall highlight behavior is obvious.
- Please call out any compliance/regulatory red flags (token plaintext, retention policies) in comments.

Changelog
- 2025-09-10: initial draft, Variant A notes and rough backlog.
- 2025-09-26: added Variant B swimlane idea and keyboard interactions after design sync.
- 2025-10-05: added PRD-level acceptance criteria for modal and updated backlog priorities.

Unresolved: legal on plaintext display, alignment algorithm for multi-request diff.
